msContents.summary: Fragments of several New Testament manuscripts in Coptic and Greek collected by Charles Godfrey Woide.

history.acquisition: Deposited with the Bodleian Library in 1885; deposit converted to a gift, 1922.

recordHist.source: Catalogued after digitisation by Peter Toth, based on Franz-Jürgen Schmitz and Gerd Mink, Liste der koptischen Handschriften des Neuen Testaments. Bd. I, Tl. 1: Die sahidischen Handschriften der Evangelien", Berlin, Boston: De Gruyter, 1986. and on Henry Ford and Charles Godfrey Woide, Appendix ad editionem Novi Testamenti Græci e Codice MS. Alexandrino a Carolo Godofredo Woide descripti, in qua continentur fragmenta Novi Testamenti juxta interpretationem dialecti Superioris Ægypti quæ Thebaidica vel Sahidica appellatur, e codicibus Oxoniensibus maxima ex parte desumpta, cum dissertatione de versione Bibliorum Ægyptiaca. Quibus subjicitur codicis Vaticani collatio, e typographeo Clarendoniano, Oxford, 1799, pp. 23–24..

msPart.head: Fragments from a Coptic Gospel book

extent.note: The intercolumn space is approximately 15 mm. Margins: upper 30–35 mm; lower 40–50 mm; inner 20–30 mm; outer 15–25 mm.

handDesc.handNote: Written in a somewhat awkward but elegant hand. The script is frequently faded and difficult to read. Beginning of Matthew 1.1–2 has been partly retraced by a less practised hand.

decoDesc.decoNote: Four initials, or possibly five including the initial at the damaged beginning of 1.1, are slightly set out at 1.1, 2.1, 3.1, and 4.1 and are clearly emphasized.
Occasional small, simple coronis and obelus signs occur before passages.

additions.p: Pagination is partly preserved, slightly indented or projecting beyond the column margin and simply framed on all sides. The four leaves are more or less torn at the outer margin; the first leaf is additionally damaged at the upper and inner margin, affecting up to seven lines. All leaves are further damaged in places, and the leaf edges are irregularly torn.

history.provenance: Other parts of the original manuscript, now identified as SA 102, are preserved in various collections. For a full list of these fragments and a description of the original volume, see SMR-Datenbank koptischer neutestamentlicher Handschriften. Please note that in literature these fragments are described as Fragment 3 but they are Fragment 1 in the current volume.

msPart.head: Fragments from a Coptic Gospel book

extent.note: Each page contains 32 lines. The original foliation is small and slender, placed above the column margin; it is faded on the recto and more clearly legible on the verso, and appears to have been entered or supplemented by a second hand.
Intercolumn space is approximately 25 mm. Margins: upper 20–45 mm; lower 40–60 mm; inner 25–35 mm; outer 50–65 mm.

supportDesc.foliation: Original folio numbering is preserved, running from ⲛⲑ to ⲝⲏ (59–68). The numerals are faded on the recto and more clearly legible on the verso.

handDesc.handNote: The script is slightly faded. Corrections are very rare; examples include erasure of a superfluous letter at Mt 16.27 and at Mt 18.10, and a correction at Mt 18.10 involving the erasure of a letter and the addition of a stroke. The form of the initial writing and the corrections suggests that the text was copied by one hand and subsequently revised by a second or third hand.

decoDesc.decoNote: A maximum of 4 initials occur in each column. They are lightly enlarged, sometimes extending over more than 2-3 lines, and are set out wholly or partly without ornament. At Mt 18.3 and Mt 19.1 the initials extend over approximately 5 lines and contain internal decoration but no further ornament.

additions.p: All five leaves are substantially complete in their textual extent, although fol. 66 is slightly damaged by smudging. The leaf edges are partly and in places considerably torn, and the writing is slightly washed out.

history.provenance: Other parts of the original manuscript, now identified as SA 104, are preserved in various collections . For a full list of these fragments and a description of the original volume, see SMR-Datenbank koptischer neutestamentlicher Handschriften. Please note that in literature these fragments are described as Fragment 4 but they are is Fragment 2 in the current volume.

msPart.head: Fragment from a Coptic Gospel book

extent.note: Margins: upper 35–45 mm; lower 50–60 mm; inner 30–40 mm; outer 45–60 mm.

handDesc.handNote: The script is an elegant, large hand. The first page preserves traces of earlier letters in the upper margin; the text is written in a single column.

history.provenance: Other parts of the original manuscript, now identified as SA 109, are preserved in various collections. For a full list of these fragments and a description of the original volume, see SMR-Datenbank koptischer neutestamentlicher Handschriften. Please note that in literature this fragments is described as Fragment 5 but it is Fragment 3 in the current volume.

msPart.head: Fragment from a Coptic Gospel book

extent.note: Margins: upper 25–35 mm; lower 35–55 mm; inner 20–30 mm; outer 20–35 mm.

supportDesc.foliation: Original foliation survives as ⲛⲑ (59) and ⲝ (60).

handDesc.handNote: The strokes of the letters are slender.

decoDesc.decoNote: Small floral ornaments occur occasionally in the margins, especially before capital letters, painted in vermilion.
Letters at the upper margin of the second page are enclosed between two horizontal lines.

additions.p: Ammonian Section numbers λε and λζ are present.

history.provenance: Other parts of the original manuscript, now identified as SA 123, are preserved in various collections . For a full list of these fragments and a description of the original volume, see SMR-Datenbank koptischer neutestamentlicher Handschriften. Please note that here these fragments are described as Fragment 6 but it is Fragment 4 in the current volume.

msPart.head: Fragments from a bilingual Coptic-Greek Gospel Book

extent.note: Each page contains 35 lines. The intercolumn space is approximately 25 mm. Margins: upper 20–45 mm; lower 40–55 mm; inner 25–35 mm; outer 50–65 mm.

The eight leaves are complete in their textual extent, although the first leaf is severely torn in the inner column; the remaining leaves only have slight text damage. The leaf edges are torn to varying degrees, and the script is occasionally washed out, blurred, and slightly offset through the parchment.
The fragements preserve the complete quire 35, as indicated by the quire numbering at the beginning and end of the sequence.

supportDesc.foliation: Original pagination is preserved, running from 469/470 to 483/484. The numbers are small and slender, placed above the column margin; on the recto they are occasionally slightly displaced and are simply framed on all sides.

handDesc.handNote: The letters are small and fine. The Coptic and Greek texts appear to have been written by the same scribe.

decoDesc.decoNote: A maximum of three initials occur in one column, extending over one or two lines, either wholly or partly, and are slightly enlarged without additional ornament.

additions.note: At f. 473, corresponding to Luke 12.29–30, parts of sentences were initially written twice, then crossed out and partly marked with dots above the letters.

history.provenance: From the same manuscript as Fragment 7 in this same volume. Other parts of the original manuscript, now identified as SA 105, are preserved in various collections . For a full list of these fragments and a description of the original volume, see SMR-Datenbank koptischer neutestamentlicher Handschriften. Please note that in literature these fragments are described as Fragment 7 but they are Fragment 5 in the current volume.

msPart.head: Fragments from a Coptic Gospel book

extent.note: The margins are partly and in places considerably torn; the script is slightly washed out in places. A water stain increases towards the outer column, and on fols. 230–234 between one and six lines at the lower part of the pages are entirely illegible.

supportDesc.foliation: Original foliation: ⲥⲕⲅ/ⲥⲕⲇ–ⲥⲗⲅ/ⲥⲗⲇ (223/224–233/234). The numerals are written above the column margin with an overline, slightly projecting beyond it.

handDesc.handNote: The script is occasionally faded. The form and execution of the writing indicate the involvement of three scribes.

decoDesc.decoNote: A maximum of four initials occur in each column. They vary in size, some being enlarged considerably and extending over several lines; they are set out wholly or partly and are generally emphasized by simple decorative treatment. Some initials are accompanied by small coronis-like signs.
On pp. 223, 225, 227 and 231 a serpentine/fletched ornament occurs above the intercolumn space; on p. 223 the first initial is also decorated with a small, simple frieze.
On pp. 223, 225, 227 and 231 there are additional ornamental flourishes; on p. 225 a simple animal or zoomorphic figure occurs in the lower part of the page.

history.provenance: Other parts of the original manuscript, now identified as SA 112, are preserved in various collections. For a full list of these fragments and a description of the original volume, see SMR-Datenbank koptischer neutestamentlicher Handschriften. Please note that in literature these fragments are described as Fragment 8 but they are Fragment 6 in the current volume.

msPart.head: Fragment from a bilingual Coptic-Greek Gospel book

msItem.title: Gospel of John (fragment)
msItem.note: John 8.22b–32b in Coptic on the recto; John 8.33a–42b in Greek on the verso.

extent.note: The page contains 35 lines. The intercolumn space is approximately 25 mm. Margins: upper approximately 35–40 mm; lower approximately 5 mm; inner approximately 25 mm; outer approximately 55–65 mm.

The surviving leaf is damaged, with the lower margin torn away. The recto nevertheless retains almost the complete writing area, while on the verso only a narrow margin remains. The inner column is slightly torn at the lower edge over approximately five lines, with the loss of one to three letters. The leaf is also affected by smaller tears and water stains.

supportDesc.foliation: Original pagination: ⲭⲛⲍ/ⲭⲛⲏ (657/658), slightly reduced in size, written slightly beyond the column margin and marked with an overline. Quire numbering on the recto gives ⲙⲅ (4th quire), likewise slightly displaced beyond the column margin.

handDesc.handNote: The script is generally well preserved on the verso and somewhat less well preserved on the recto.

decoDesc.decoNote: One or two initials occur in each column. They are enlarged to varying degrees and set out without ornament.

additions.p: A correction or addition by the first hand occurs on the recto.

history.provenance: From the same manuscript as Fragment 5 in this same volume. Other parts of the original manuscript, now identified as SA 105, are preserved in various collections . For a full list of these fragments and a description of the original volume, see SMR-Datenbank koptischer neutestamentlicher Handschriften. Please note that in literature the fragments is described as Fragment 9 but it is Fragment 7 in the current volume.

msPart.head: Fragments from a Coptic Gospel book

extent.note: Each page contains 34–38 lines. The intercolumn space is approximately 25–30 mm. Margins: upper 25–30 mm; lower 15–35 mm.

All four leaves are damaged to varying degrees at the edges. The margins are in places considerably torn, especially at the inner margin. The first leaf is more severely damaged; the writing is occasionally affected by dirt and water stains.

supportDesc.foliation: Original pagination: ⲧⲍ/ⲧⲏ–ⲧⲓⲅ/ⲧⲓⲇ (307/308–313/314), slightly reduced in size and projecting slightly beyond the column margin, with an overline.

handDesc.handNote: A relatively less elegant and neat script occasionally affected by dirt and water stains.

decoDesc.decoNote: One to three initials occur in each column. They are lightly enlarged, sometimes extending over more than three lines, and are wholly or partly set out. They are simple, usually without ornament, and occasionally accompanied by a small coloured coronis.
Some more elaborate initials are coloured and extend over four to seven lines, with internal patterning and tendril work.

history.provenance: Other parts of the original manuscript, now identified as SA 103, are preserved in various collections. For a full list of these fragments and a description of the original volume, see SMR-Datenbank koptischer neutestamentlicher Handschriften. Please note that in literature the fragments are described as Fragment 10 but they are Fragment 8 in the current volume.

msPart.head: Fragment from a bilingual Coptic-Greek Apostolos (Acts and Pauline Epistles)

extent.note: Dimensions recorded are of the original manuscript reconstructed from the surviving fragments.
Margins: upper 30–40 mm; lower 80–95 mm; inner 25–30 mm; outer 60–75 mm.

handDesc.handNote: Rounded very neatly executed hand wiritng both the Coptic and the Greek text.

history.provenance: Other parts of the original manuscript, now identified as SA 35, are preserved in various collections. For a full list of these fragments and a description of the original volume, see SMR-Datenbank koptischer neutestamentlicher Handschriften. Please note that in literature the fragments are described as Fragment 11 but they are Fragment 9 in the current volume.

msPart.head: Fragments from a Coptic Apostolos (Acts and Pauline Epistles)

handDesc.handNote: Slender, straight Coptic hand, with larger letters at the beginning of sections with larger undecorated initials at the beginning of sections. The Coptic title ⲧⲉⲡⲣⲟⲥ ϩⲣⲱⲙⲁⲓⲟⲥ is written above the columns.

decoDesc.decoNote: Occasional larger coloured initials and marginal decorative elements.

additions.note: Old Testament quotations are marked with a diple in the margin.

msPart.head: Fragment from a Coptic Apostolos (Acts and Apuline Epistles)

msItem.note: These fragments seem have been misidentified in the literature as belonging to a bilingual Coptic-Greek manuscript, but they are in fact in Coptic only, cf. G. Kurt Aland, Berlin, Boston: De Gruyter, 1969, pp. 218–265..

supportDesc.foliation: Original foliation: ⲛⲅ (53) at the beginning and ⲍ (60) at the end.

decoDesc.decoNote: Small floral ornaments in red and green, placed before capital letters, frequently occur in the margins.
